title: Orbital network fabric: Terra blueprint for resilient VPC topology and egress orchestration
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver a reusable Terraform module and CI-driven patterns for Redwood Private VPC networking that standardize subnet roles, multi-az NAT/IGW egress, enforced VPC endpoints (S3/Dynamo/SecretsManager), and routing guardrails. This module (orbital-network-fabric) should make private deployments predictable to provision, straightforward to upgrade, and observable for egress health and routing correctness.

Scope: module inputs/outputs for subnet role mapping (control/compute/data), AZ-aware NAT pools and fallback IGW behavior, private VPC endpoint construction with policy attachments, explicit route table constructs for prefix lists, and optional service egress proxies. Also includes an upgrade strategy (state drift detection, canary apply plan, preflight checks) and runtime health checks (synthetic probes and route validation) wired to our Console dashboards.

Non-goals: Do not attempt provider-agnostic abstractions (AWS-only for this iteration). This module will not replace customer-specific overlay routing; instead it offers recommended sane defaults and opt-outs.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes clear inputs for AZ count, subnet CIDR templates, NAT vs IGW egress policy, and list of required managed VPC endpoints
Module creates per-AZ NAT gateway pairs with automated failover route propagation and documented cost profile
Built-in Terraform plan-time checks to prevent overlapping CIDRs or subnets crossing AZ boundaries
Post-deploy synthetic health probe Lambda (or container) validates egress path and endpoint reachability and emits metrics to CloudWatch/Console
A safe upgrade path documented: preflight plan checks, canary apply to a single AZ, automated rollback on health regression, and runbook links
Unit/integration tests in CI: terraform validate, terraforming plan diffs against known fixtures, and acceptance tests hitting a test endpoint via private route
tasks: Draft initial module interface and variable set
Implement subnet role mapping and route table attachments
Add NAT/IGW orchestration with optional paired standby NATs for AZ failover
Implement VPC endpoint creation with policy attachment templates and optional prefix-list sourcing
Create terraform plan-time sanity checks using pre-apply validation scripts
Author synthetic egress probe and CloudWatch metric emitter
Integrate module into infra-ci pipeline with plan checks and canary apply job
Write upgrade playbook and rollback automation steps
Create Console dashboard for egress health and routing anomalies

notes: Design trade-offs: Pairing NAT per AZ increases cost but reduces cross-AZ egress latency and single-point-of-failure risk. Default is paired NATs; customers can opt for IGW-only cheaper config.
Routing guardrails: We implement explicit route table resources instead of relying on implicit gateway attachments so that plans are deterministic and easier to audit.
Upgrade strategy: Use a three-step canary (plan-only -> apply in single AZ -> monitor 30min -> rollout remaining AZs) with automatic rollback on health regression metrics.

Healthcheck implementation: Probe will perform outbound fetch to a small signed object in S3 via private endpoint and verify response headers and TLS; it will also validate that route tables contain expected prefixes. Failures surface to Console and trigger runbook alert.
